## Overview

This project models how **enterprise IT teams** combine **service desk ticketing** with **Active Directory (AD)** and **Windows server** operations. Every request—new hire account, server CPU alert, offboarding disable—is tracked in a ticket with priority, assignee, and optional links to `server_hostname` and `ad_sam`. A **mock AD layer** (SQLite) mirrors real cmdlets (`New-ADUser`, `Disable-ADAccount`, `Add-ADGroupMember`) so you can practice safely on Linux or macOS before running scripts on a domain controller.

**GitHub (source code):** [sophalchan/it-service-desk-ad-automation](https://github.com/sophalchan/it-service-desk-ad-automation)

**Stack:** Python · Flask · SQLite · PowerShell (optional, for real Windows AD)

## Background of the Study

Small and mid-size organizations run on **Windows Server** roles—domain controllers, file servers, application hosts—and **Active Directory** as the identity store. Help desk and infrastructure teams receive a steady mix of requests: provision a contractor account, add someone to **VPN** or **Engineering** security groups, investigate **SRV-APP01** performance, or **disable** an account after HR offboarding. Without a system of record, work happens in email threads and chat messages; audits fail, SLAs slip, and AD changes are disconnected from *why* they were made.

**IT service management (ITSM)** introduces **tickets** as the single workflow object: who asked, what server or SAM account is involved, priority, status, and notes. **Identity lifecycle management** ties HR events to AD operations. This lab compresses that real-world pattern into a teachable, runnable stack—appropriate for **IT/IoT** portfolios, CySA+ study, or anyone moving from pure development into **infrastructure and operations**.

The design reflects experience teaching **Information Technology** (M.S. IT, PSU) and supporting engineering teams where **traceability** (ticket → AD action → server) matters as much as speed.

## Motivation of the Study

- **Connect tickets to infrastructure** — link each request to `server_hostname` and/or `ad_sam` for clear context  
- **Practice AD workflows safely** — mock directory on SQLite; optional PowerShell for production domains  
- **Learn REST APIs for IT tools** — same pattern as ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, or internal portals  
- **Prepare for real AD cmdlets** — lab endpoints map 1:1 to `New-ADUser`, `Disable-ADAccount`, `Add-ADGroupMember`  
- **Dashboard visibility** — open tickets, critical queue, counts by category (AD vs Server vs Network)  
- **Ship a portfolio-ready repo** — clone, seed data, curl the API in minutes  

## Tools & Components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `data/servers.json` | Catalog of DC, file, and app servers (hostname, role, OS) |
| `data/ad_users_seed.json` | Initial AD users for the mock forest |
| `src/database.py` | SQLite schema: `ad_users`, `tickets`, `ticket_notes` |
| `src/ad_service.py` | List/create/disable users; add to security groups |
| `src/ticket_service.py` | Create tickets, update status, dashboard stats |
| `app.py` | Flask REST API (port **8091**) |
| `scripts/init_lab.py` | Seed sample tickets (onboarding, server alert, offboarding) |
| `scripts/ticket_cli.py` | Command-line ticket list/create |
| `powershell/New-AdLabUser.ps1` | Production-style user creation on Windows |
| `powershell/Disable-AdLabUser.ps1` | Production-style account disable |

## Step-by-Step Workflow

### Step 1 — Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sophalchan/it-service-desk-ad-automation.git
cd it-service-desk-ad-automation
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Step 2 — Initialize the lab database

```bash
python scripts/init_lab.py
```

This creates `data/tickets.db`, loads seed AD users, and inserts three sample tickets (new hire AD, high CPU on **SRV-APP01**, disable terminated account).

### Step 3 — Start the API

```bash
python app.py
```

Open `http://localhost:8091/health` — you should see `{"status": "ok", ...}`.

### Step 4 — Review the dashboard

```bash
curl http://localhost:8091/dashboard
```

Note `open_tickets`, `critical_open`, and `by_category` (e.g. **Active Directory** vs **Server**).

### Step 5 — List servers and AD users

```bash
curl http://localhost:8091/servers
curl http://localhost:8091/ad/users
curl "http://localhost:8091/ad/users?enabled_only=true"
```

### Step 6 — Create a ticket (new request)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8091/tickets \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Grant VPN access for remote engineer",
    "description": "Add jsmith to VPN-Users after manager approval.",
    "category": "Access",
    "priority": "Medium",
    "requester": "manager@corp.local",
    "server_hostname": "SRV-DC01",
    "ad_sam": "jsmith",
    "assigned_to": "helpdesk"
  }'
```

### Step 7 — Perform AD operations (linked to ticket work)

**Create user:**

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8091/ad/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "sam": "jsmith",
    "display_name": "Jane Smith",
    "email": "jsmith@corp.local",
    "ou": "OU=Users,DC=corp,DC=local",
    "groups": ["Domain Users", "VPN-Users"]
  }'
```

**Add to group:**

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8091/ad/users/jsmith/groups \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"group": "Engineering"}'
```

**Disable user (offboarding):**

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8091/ad/users/temp_user/disable
```

### Step 8 — Update ticket status (close the loop)

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8091/tickets/1 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "status": "Resolved",
    "note": "AD account created and added to VPN-Users.",
    "author": "helpdesk"
  }'
```

Valid statuses: `Open`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`, `Closed`.

### Step 9 — CLI alternative

```bash
python scripts/ticket_cli.py list
python scripts/ticket_cli.py create \
  --title "Patch Tuesday reboot window" \
  --desc "Schedule maintenance on SRV-FILE01" \
  --category Server \
  --priority Low \
  --requester "server-ops@corp.local" \
  --server SRV-FILE01
```

### Step 10 — Move to real Active Directory (Windows)

On a domain controller or RSAT workstation, adapt the included PowerShell:

```powershell
.\powershell\New-AdLabUser.ps1 -SamAccountName jsmith -DisplayName "Jane Smith" -Email "jsmith@corp.local"
.\powershell\Disable-AdLabUser.ps1 -SamAccountName temp_user
```

Always run AD changes **only after** the matching ticket is approved—same discipline as in production ITSM.

## Architecture

```text
Requester (HR, monitoring, user)
    → POST /tickets (category, priority, server_hostname, ad_sam)
    → Help desk / server-ops assignment
    → POST /ad/users | /disable | /groups  (mock AD or PowerShell on DC)
    → PATCH /tickets (status + audit note in ticket_notes)
    → GET /dashboard (queue metrics)
```

## What You Learn

| Topic | Lab takeaway |
|-------|----------------|
| ITSM basics | Ticket lifecycle, priorities, categories |
| Active Directory | SAM accounts, OUs, security groups, enable/disable |
| Server ops | Inventory-driven hostname references in tickets |
| APIs | REST design for internal IT automation |
| Security mindset | Offboarding = disable AD + documented ticket note |

## Limitations (Honest Notes)

- Mock AD is **not** LDAP or Kerberos—use PowerShell samples for real forests  
- No RBAC on API endpoints—add auth before any production deployment  
- SQLite is single-file; scale-out would use PostgreSQL + real CMDB integration
